findings.summary: URLs in urlset entries that fail Url::parse() are silently dropped, while the original JS code unconditionally passed all non-file, non-xml URLs to the urlsHandler callback.
findings.failure_scenario: A sitemap contains <url><loc>https://example.com/path with spaces</loc></url>. The unencoded spaces cause Url::parse to fail. The URL is silently dropped — it falls into neither xml_sitemaps nor valid_urls. The _process_sitemap function returns Ok without error, so the JS caller never knows the URL was lost and never triggers the JS fallback logic that would have handled it.

findings.summary: The new parseSitemapXml and processSitemap methods duplicate the exact same promise/error-handling/RUSTFC:ERROR block pattern from filterLinks, creating a maintenance burden where any fix must be replicated across three nearly identical code blocks.
findings.failure_scenario: A future developer fixing a bug in the RUSTFC:ERROR prefix parsing logic (e.g., edge cases in the res.split call) fixes filterLinks but misses parseSitemapXml or processSitemap, leaving inconsistent error handling across the three FFI wrappers.
